note: Pages whose Getting-started steps or Controls block were set by hand after generation. build-arcade-gamedoc.py uses these verbatim in place of what it would derive; everything else on the page is still generated.

bzone.why: Two sticks, one per tread, and each only goes forward and back; the core's labels give each stick left and right as well.
bzone.controls:
Battlezone has two sticks, one per tread, and both are mapped. Push both the same way to drive; push one only, or push them opposite ways, to turn on the spot. Fire is the one button that matters.

GamepadKeyboardAction
Left stick↑ ↓Left tread forward / backward
Right stickI KRight tread forward / backward
AZFire

centiped.steps:
• Insert a coin — the coin slot at the top left, or 5.

  • Hold a direction rather than tapping it — this cabinet had a trackball, so movement is continuous while held.

irobot.why: The panel's two buttons were VIEW buttons wired to the start inputs, so the camera rows come from the game, not the core's labels (which list only Fire and an unused button 2; RB tested dead). Written before the hold-a-direction step.
irobot.steps:
• Insert a coin — the coin slot at the top left, or 5.
  • Press 1 player start — the 1P button, or 1.
  • The cabinet used an analogue stick, so hold a direction rather than tapping.
irobot.controls:
Fire is on the stick. The panel’s two buttons were the camera, which the game reads through the start buttons, so in play 1P lowers the view and 2P raises it.

sf1.why: The core names no buttons; the driver reads them as two pressure-sensitive groups of three, set out as punches and kicks.
sf1.controls:
Six buttons in two groups of three. The emulator’s driver reads buttons 1–3 as one control and 4–6 as another, each passing through the same pressure scale — so within a group the three buttons are the same attack at light, medium and heavy. That is Capcom’s six-button layout: punches on the first group, kicks on the second.

GamepadKeyboardAction
D-pad, or the left stick← → ↑ ↓Move, jump and crouch
AZLight punch
RBXMedium punch
XVHeavy punch
YALight kick
BCMedium kick
LBSHeavy kick

starwars.why: Four identical triggers shown as one row; written before the hold-a-direction step, which a proportional stick does not need.
starwars.steps:
• Insert a coin — the coin slot at the top left, or 5.
  • Press 1 player start — the 1P button, or 1.
  • The cabinet used a flight yoke, and the left stick is a real stand-in for it: the aim is proportional, so how far you push is how far the crosshair travels, and it returns to the centre when you let go. The movement keys and the D-pad aim it too, but at a fixed rate. Any of the four fire buttons shoots.
starwars.controls:
This cabinet used 4 buttons.

GamepadKeyboardAction
D-pad, or the left stick← → ↑ ↓Left / Right / Up / Down
A, RB, X or YZ X V AFire — the cabinet had four triggers, all the same

hangon.why: The core names no controls: throttle and brake are analogue axes Y and Z, not buttons. RT drives the throttle (bound to 'left stick up') and LT the brake (Z assigned to 'right stick down' by the default.cfg play.html writes at boot). Play-tested 12/09/2026.
hangon.controls:
No buttons on this cabinet. You sat on a motorbike: turning the handlebars steered, twisting the grip was the throttle, and a lever was the brake — three analogue controls, which the triggers and the left stick stand in for here.

GamepadKeyboardAction
Left stick← →Steer — lean into the bend
RT↑Throttle
LTKBrake

sharrier.why: Play-tested 13/09/2026. Centres correctly on the core's defaults, and the stick is proportional, so the generic hold-a-direction step is wrong for it — that step is for a cabinet whose analogue port is driven from a D-pad. The core's data labels all three buttons Shot; only the first one fires, which matches the cabinet's single trigger, so the page lists one.
sharrier.steps:
• Insert a coin — the coin slot at the top left, or 5.
  • Press 1 player start — the 1P button, or 1.
  • The cabinet was a flight stick, and the left stick stands in for it properly: how far you push is how fast Harrier moves, and he stops where you leave him when you let go. The movement keys and the D-pad steer him too, but at one fixed speed. Z, or A on the pad, fires.
sharrier.controls:
The cabinet had a single trigger on its flight stick. The emulator’s data lists three buttons, all named Shot, but only the first one fires.

GamepadKeyboardAction
D-pad, or the left stick← → ↑ ↓Left / Right / Up / Down
AZShot

sinistar.why: Play-tested 13/09/2026. Centres correctly on the core's defaults and steers proportionally, so no option changes and no hold-a-direction step. The Sinibomb was documented on RB and does nothing there: the core binds this game's Button 2 to retropad L, which this site's pad map sends to B on the pad and C on the keyboard. Read out of the core's own input list in MAME's setup menu, then confirmed at the pad. The page's own map assumes MAME button 2 arrives on retropad Y, which is true of other cabinets but not this one.
sinistar.steps:
• Insert a coin — the coin slot at the top left, or 5.
  • Press 1 player start — the 1P button, or 1.
  • The cabinet used a 49-way stick, and the left stick stands in for it: how far you push is how fast the ship flies, and it holds its heading when you let go. The movement keys and the D-pad fly it too, but at one fixed speed. Z fires; C throws a Sinibomb.
sinistar.controls:
This cabinet used 2 buttons.

GamepadKeyboardAction
D-pad, or the left stick← → ↑ ↓Left / Right / Up / Down
AZFire
BCSinibomb
